articles.description:
1️⃣ WebSocket কী? HTTP থেকে কীভাবে আলাদা?
সহজ উত্তর:
কল্পনা করো তুমি তোমার বন্ধুকে চিঠি পাঠাচ্ছো।
HTTP হলো চিঠির মতো:
তুমি → চিঠি পাঠালে → বন্ধু পড়লো → জবাব দিলো → শেষ
(প্রতিবার নতুন চিঠি = নতুন connection)

WebSocket হলো ফোন কলের মতো:
তুমি → ফোন করলে → লাইন খোলা রইলো → যেকোনো সময় কথা বলো
(একবার connect = সবসময় connected)

HTTP:
Browser  →→→ Request →→→  Server
Browser  ←←← Response ←←← Server
(connection বন্ধ!)

WebSocket:
Browser  ←——————————————→  Server
         (সবসময় open থাকে)
         যেকোনো সময় data
         দুইদিক থেকেই যেতে পারে

2️⃣ Laravel Reverb কী? Pusher থেকে কীভাবে আলাদা?

Pusher হলো ভাড়া করা ফোন সার্ভিসের মতো — তুমি টাকা দাও, তারা সব manage করে।

articles.author: Prince Sharma
articles.description:
One thing I’ve noticed in the developer world is how many projects get abandoned too quickly.
A developer gets an idea.
For the first few days, progress feels fast and motivating.
Then reality hits.
Bugs appear.
And that’s the moment when many projects quietly die.
But the difference between a finished product and an abandoned project is usually not skill.
It’s persistence.
Almost every useful tool or product went through a phase where building it felt slow, messy, and frustrating.
The developers who succeed are often just the ones who keep going when the excitement fades.
Because most projects don’t fail due to bad ideas.
They fail because people stop building. 🚀
articles.title: Most Developers Quit Projects Too Early

You’ve built a linear LangGraph. It works, but it feels like an assembly line in a world that needs a smart traffic controller. You know the feeling: your AI agent follows the exact same steps every single time, even when the input screams for a different path. It’s inefficient, it’s brittle, and it’s not how complex systems are meant to work.

Why accuracy alone is not enough and how organizations can audit AI systems before regulators, attackers, or users expose the failures.
Artificial intelligence systems are now embedded in decisions that affect people’s lives credit approvals, fraud detection, hiring, underwriting, and customer support automation. But while AI adoption has accelerated rapidly, governance frameworks have struggled to keep up. Most organizations still test AI systems using traditional software testing practices. That approach fails because AI systems behave differently. Traditional software is deterministic: the same input produces the same output every time. AI systems are probabilistic. They learn patterns from data, adapt to new inputs, and may produce different outputs across interactions.
From a governan…

articles.author: MFS CORP
articles.description:
If you're into Pokémon, you know the pain. News drops across a dozen sites — Serebii, PokeBeach, PokeJungle, NintendoLife, Dexerto — and by the time you check them all, you've already missed something.
So I automated it.
A Telegram channel called Pokémon News Pulse that aggregates news from 14 different sources and delivers it every 15 minutes. One feed, everything you need.
Here's everything it monitors:
Dedicated Pokémon Sites:
Serebii.net (scraped — no RSS available)
PokeBeach.com (scraped — RSS blocked)
PokeJungle
PokePatch
Pokémon GO Hub
Gaming News (filtered for Pokémon):
Dexerto
NintendoLife
NintendoEverything
ScreenRant
IGN
Kotaku
Polygon
GameSpot
Search Queries (SearXNG):
"Pokémon news today"
"Pokémon TCG Pocket news"
"Pokémon GO update news"
"Pokémon Legends news"
"Pokémon games announcement"
"Pokémon anime news"
Every 15 minutes, a Python script:
Pulls the latest stories from all 14 RSS feeds
Scrapes Serebii and PokeBeach directly (they block RSS)
Runs 6 search queries to catch anything RSS missed
Filters mainstream sites — only Pokémon-related stories pass through
Deduplicates by title hash — no repeats
Only posts stories from the last hour — always fresh
Extracts article images for visual posts
Posts to the Telegram channel with source links
🎮 Game announcements and updates
🃏 TCG Pocket and card game news
📱 Pokémon GO events, raids, community days
🎬 Anime and movie updates
🏆 Competitive VGC and tournament results
Every post includes the headline, a brief description, an image from the article, and a direct link to the source.
Instant delivery — push notifications as news breaks
No algorithm — you see everything, in order
Free — no subscription, no ads
Clean — one story per message, no clutter
t.me/PokemonNewsPulse — join and you'll start getting updates within 15 minutes.
We also run channels for other topics:
🤖 AI & Tech News

🌍 World News

₿ Crypto Markets






Built by MFS Corp. Part of the Building MFS Corp series.
articles.title: I Built a Telegram Channel That Monitors 14 Pokémon News Sources Every 15 Minutes
